strategy: breadth-first evidence mapping across all eight candidate cores, followed by risk-driven deep dives and cross-core synthesis

rounds.name: Ontology challenge scan
rounds.purpose: Test whether each core is conceptually coherent, separable, and missing fundamental mechanisms.
rounds.stop: Every core has definitions, competing constructs, and explicit split/merge/missing-core hypotheses.

rounds.name: Evidence landscape
rounds.purpose: Collect highest-level reviews/meta-analyses and foundational primary studies for all eight cores.
rounds.stop: Every core has coverage across definition, mechanism, evidence, moderators, measurement, contradictions, and transfer limits.

rounds.name: Mechanism decomposition
rounds.purpose: Derive evidence-backed modules and candidate neurons without arbitrary count targets.
rounds.stop: Major mechanism families are represented and overlap is explicitly resolved or flagged.

rounds.name: Cross-core edge synthesis
rounds.purpose: Test material connections, mediators, moderators, inhibition, feedback, and competing explanations.
rounds.stop: Every strong edge has claim-level evidence and every high-impact hypothesized edge has a research status.

rounds.name: Measurement and transport audit
rounds.purpose: Map validated instruments/behavioral measures/proxies and assess transfer to social-media contexts.
rounds.stop: No latent construct is inferred from a platform metric without ambiguity/alternative-explanation metadata.

rounds.name: Disconfirmation and saturation
rounds.purpose: Search nulls, contradictions, failed replications, heterogeneity, boundary conditions, and cultural/contextual limits.
rounds.stop: Two consecutive targeted search passes yield no structural change, no new critical contradiction, and only marginal refinement.

global_questions: What is the construct, and what is it explicitly not?
What competing definitions or taxonomies exist?
What mechanisms are causally supported versus merely associated?
What moderators and boundary conditions materially change the effect?
What individual, social, cultural, temporal, and platform contexts limit transport?
How is the construct measured, and what validity/reliability evidence exists?
What null, contradictory, or replication evidence exists?
Which other cores does this construct interact with, through what mechanism?
Could the observed social-media behavior be explained by a different core or non-psychological platform process?
inclusion: Human research directly relevant to the construct or its mechanism.
Meta-analyses, systematic reviews, high-quality narrative/theoretical reviews for map building.
Preregistered/replicated experiments and strong primary experiments for causal claims.
Longitudinal/behavioral/large observational studies when causal experiments are infeasible.
Foundational older research when still theoretically central.
Social-media-specific studies when they measure constructs with acceptable clarity.
exclusion: Marketing blogs, creator advice, SEO listicles, and unsourced pop psychology as scientific evidence.
Claims supported only by search snippets without opening the source.
Non-human evidence used as direct proof of human social-media behavior.
Neuroimaging findings treated as behavioral causation without matching behavioral evidence.
Platform metric correlations presented as latent psychological measurements without construct-validity support.
Duplicate studies/reports unless needed for correction/version history.

attention.ontology_challenge: Is Attention one coherent core or a family requiring modules for selection, control, salience, history, and sustained engagement?

curiosity.ontology_challenge: Separate curiosity from novelty, uncertainty, information value, surprise, and general reward seeking.

valuation_emotion.ontology_challenge: Test whether Valuation and Emotion can remain one core family or should become separate top-level cores.

identity.ontology_challenge: Separate personal identity, social identity, self-relevance, norms, self-presentation, and homophily.

trust.ontology_challenge: Separate trust from credibility, expertise, authenticity, familiarity, liking, and perceived benevolence.

connection.ontology_challenge: Separate parasocial interaction, parasocial relationship, familiarity, attachment, identification, and real reciprocity.

social_transmission.ontology_challenge: Separate observed sharing behavior from motives such as emotion, utility, identity signaling, reputation, norms, and relationship maintenance.

reinforcement_habit.ontology_challenge: Test whether reinforcement learning and habit belong in one core or require separate top-level anchors; distinguish recurrence from habit.

cross_core_priority_questions: Attention ↔ Valuation/Reinforcement: when does learned value bias selection, and how large/context-bound is the effect?
Curiosity ↔ Valuation: when is information itself valuable, and when does uncertainty cause avoidance instead?
Identity ↔ Trust/Connection: are similarity effects mediated by liking, credibility, belonging, or other constructs?
Trust ↔ Connection: what is directional versus correlational?
Emotion/Valuation → Transmission: which dimensions matter and under what content/social contexts?
Connection/Trust → Return: distinguish relationship value, deliberate utility, reminders, and habit.
Identity → Transmission: separate norm compliance, signaling, self-presentation, and group relevance.
Transmission → Attention: distinguish psychological effect from mechanical exposure created by platform/network distribution.

structural_change_events: new moderator that changes edge direction
new causal pathway that changes reasoning
saturation.practical_saturation_rule: After broad coverage, run at least two targeted disconfirmation/gap passes. A unit can close only when neither pass produces a structural change event and new evidence mainly refines already represented mechanisms.
saturation.reopen_rule: Any later high-quality evidence that triggers a structural change event reopens only affected nodes/edges and descendants.
